Every run read SKILL.md first (#1). Tool calls are numbered once per tool_use id; each transcript repeats some tool_use blocks, and the repeats are not counted. opus-1 also invoked superpowers:test-driven-development (#13) and wrote its tests before the code.

Rules changed since d04061d (git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/). Of this case's seven rules only Chain fallible steps with `with` changed. Its verdicts are decided by this sentence of SKILL.md, under the heading "Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function": "One step is a `with` only when its body cannot fail and there is no `else`, so the `with` does nothing but pass the error through; any other one-step `with` is a `case`." A pass-through `case` is now the shape to replace, by the same rule: "A `case` whose error clause is `{:error, _reason} = error -> error` is the same pass-through spelled out over four lines; write it as the `with`." The earlier standard (a one-step with is a violation, a case for a single fallible call is not exercised) no longer applies. The other six rules and the Formatting bullet are unchanged and are graded to the 2026-10-23 standard: a passing --check-formatted after a file's last edit counts as formatted for Before you finish step 1; a mix test that compiled the app with no warnings counts as the compile step; a total that raises KeyError on an unpriced SKU is clean when its @doc covers it; Map.put/3 on the inner items map inside %{cart | items: ...} is not the forbidden pattern; a code kept as a string and checked against a literal list is clean under the atom rule.

Chain fallible steps with `with`: 0 of 5 violated (2026-10-23: 1 of 5, sonnet-1, for a one-step with). Four runs wrote one-step with blocks with no else and a body that cannot fail: opus-1 lines 77-79, haiku-2 lines 58-60, sonnet-1 lines 96-98 (beside a two-step with at lines 74-77), sonnet-2 lines 65-67 and 89-92. None wrote a pass-through case, an else, or a nested fallible case. haiku-1 checks membership with if (line 57): not exercised. Against 2026-10-23, opus moves from not exercised to clean, haiku from not exercised to clean (haiku-2), sonnet from violated to clean. The code shape barely moved: three runs here write the one-step with where three runs in 2026-10-23 wrote the pass-through case the rule now replaces. Under the old text this sweep would have had four violating runs.

Per-file formatting check line: met in 1 of 5 (opus-1), the same as 2026-10-23. opus-1 edited the test file (#16, #17) and checked it alone (#19) before mix test (#20), wrote cart.ex (#21) and checked it alone (#22) before compiling, then edited cart.ex twice (#26, #27) and checked it alone again (#28). haiku-1: Write cart.ex (#4), two Edits of the test file (#5, #6), then one check on both (#8) after a refused chain (#7). haiku-2: Write cart.ex (#9), two Edits of the test file (#10, #11), one check on both (#13) after a refused chain (#12). sonnet-1: a refused python3 heredoc (#4), Write cart.ex (#5), Write the test file (#6), then #7 checked each file on its own path before compile, Credo and tests. sonnet-2: a refused python3 heredoc (#4), Write cart.ex (#5), Write the test file (#6), then one check on both (#7). In every Haiku and Sonnet run cart.ex was left for the test file before any check. Every check passed on its first run and no run called mix format, so the formatter changed nothing in any run and the Formatting bullet's rewrite half was not exercised.

Before you finish: 0 of 5 violated, as in 2026-10-23. opus-1: check (#28), compile --force --warnings-as-errors (#29), full mix test (#30, 24 passed), credo --strict (#31). haiku-1: check on both (#8), mix test (#9, compiled shop with no warnings, 14 passed), credo --strict (#10). haiku-2: check on both (#13), mix test (#14, compiled with no warnings, 14 passed), credo --strict (#15). sonnet-1 and sonnet-2: one command (#7) with the check, mix compile --warnings-as-errors, credo --strict and the full suite (20 and 18 passed). No run called mix format itself; the passing checks count, per the judgement call. The Haiku runs never ran a separate compile; their mix test compiled the app with no warnings, which counts.

Other graded rules. Atoms: opus-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 use one parse clause per code string (haiku-2 after trimming and upcasing); haiku-1 keeps the trimmed, upcased string and checks it against @codes ["SAVE10", "FREESHIP"] (lines 13, 57), clean as in earlier grades. defstruct: bare atoms in all five ([:items, :discount] in three, [:items, :code] in haiku-1, [:items, :discount_code] in haiku-2). Return tuples: atom or tagged-tuple reasons everywhere; opus-1 and haiku-2 raise KeyError on an unpriced SKU and say so in the @doc; haiku-1 raises KeyError and its @doc names no exception but states that `prices` maps each SKU in the cart to its price (line 67), which makes a missing price a caller bug, so I counted it clean; both Sonnet runs return {:error, {:unknown_sku, sku}}. Money: integer div in all five; opus-1 rounds the discounted subtotal down, the others round halves up. Naming: domain names throughout; no boolean, get, fetch, size or length functions.

other_violations, all under rules outside this case's list. haiku-1 pipes two steps on one line (cart.ex line 55) and writes an if with do: and else: branches on their own lines (lines 39-41), which the changed do: rule says to write as do ... end. Both Haiku test files have bare arrange matches that can fail and a bind-then-== check, the shapes Assert with patterns names (haiku-1 lines 68-71, 88-91, 97-100, 107-110; haiku-2 lines 72-75, 92-95, 101-104, 111-114). sonnet-1 has one inline case clause of 72 characters after indentation (cart.ex line 103), past the about-70 limit of the renamed `->` rule; the margin is small. Checked and not listed: the inline `fn` bodies inside Enum.sum_by (one expression each, which the current Readability rules keep on one line); sonnet-2's reduce_while clauses at lines 110-111 (48 and 54 characters, both bodies a tuple); the test pipelines starting with Cart.new(), which follow the project's own test file; sonnet-1's wrapped test head at test lines 90-93, written in that shape and covered by no rule, as in earlier grades. I found no break of the new Readability rules, the captures or named-argument rules, or the new describe sentence in ex_unit.md (every describe names a function).
